newsitem.title: UK: British airliner has near miss with paraglider.
newsitem.headline: British airliner has near miss with paraglider.

text.p: A passenger jet belonging to British airline easyJet had to take evasive action as it was coming in to land after the pilot spotted a motorised paraglider coming dangerously close, the airline's founder said on Monday.
Stelios Haji-Ioannou said the Boeing B-737 had been at 3,500 feet (1,100 m) just eight miles (13 km) out from Luton airport near London at the time of the incident on Saturday.
"It is very likely that the paraglider should not have been there. The air traffic controller had made no mention of any other traffic in the area," Haji-Ioannou said by telephone.
"The pilot was very experienced and took evasive action. I don't think the passengers noticed what had happened," he added. The B-737 was en route from Barcelona.
The incident came to light when the airline pilot filed a nearmiss report with Britain's Civil Aviation Authority, a sign he felt his aircraft had been at real risk.

Motorised paragliders, which have only been legal in Britain since June this year, are simple contraptions which can nevertheless reach a maximum height of around 10,000 feet (3,000 metres). Unlike microlight aircraft, they have no wheels.
An official at the British Hanggliding and Paragliding Association said action was being taken to trace the pilot, but could give no further details.
